biography:
Michel Neugarten's journey began amidst the rain-slicked karting tracks of Genk, Belgium. From the age of seven, he showed a preternatural ability to read the asphalt, anticipating grip levels with uncanny accuracy. His father, a former club racer, nurtured this talent, funding his early career through the ranks. A defining moment came at the 2018 European Karting Championship, where, despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, Neugarten carved his way through the field to finish second, showcasing his relentless determination. After a brief but successful stint in Formula Renault, Neugarten found his true calling in GT racing. He joined Lamborghini in 2021, quickly establishing himself as a dependable and consistent driver. While victories have been elusive, his steady performances and unwavering commitment have made him a valuable asset to the team. He is looking to secure more podiums in the upcoming racing season.

Neugarten's transition to GT racing wasn't without its challenges. The raw aggression of open-wheel racing had to be tempered with the patience and tire management required for endurance events. He recalls a particularly brutal 24 Hours of Spa in 2022, where a late-race puncture cost the team a potential podium finish. This experience, though painful, proved to be a turning point, forcing him to refine his approach and develop a deeper understanding of car setup. Off the track, Michel is described as a quiet and unassuming character, preferring the company of his close-knit team to the glitz and glamour of the racing world. He has remained close with his father and appreciates the support he continues to receive.

His dedication to the sport is remarkable, and he often dedicates time to mentor young racers at his old karting track. He is working hard to elevate his skill level in the coming years and close the gap with the top racers.

Currently, Neugarten is focused on refining his race craft, aiming to transform his consistent performances into race wins. He believes that with the right car and a little bit of luck, he can challenge for championships in the future.
drivingStyle: Neugarten's driving style is characterized by its smoothness and precision. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes or risky maneuvers. Instead, he focuses on maximizing corner speed, minimizing tire wear, and maintaining a consistent pace throughout the race. His ability to adapt to changing track conditions is exceptional, allowing him to extract the most from the car regardless of the weather. Tire management is one of Neugarten's greatest strengths. He is capable of running long stints at a competitive pace, preserving his tires for the crucial final laps. He analyzes every corner, and his smooth driving style allows him to excel in endurance races.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry from their karting days. Rossi, known for his aggressive driving, often clashed with Neugarten's more calculated approach.
Dubois and Neugarten were teammates briefly. Dubois was unhappy that Neugarten was given the better performing car and the two have been terse ever since.
Tanaka has accused Neugarten of unsportsmanlike conduct in the past, particularly for blocking tactics in qualifying.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky socks, knitted by his grandmother, for every race.
Listens to classical music (specifically Mozart) to calm his nerves before getting into the car.
Has a pre-race ritual of drawing a small Belgian flag on his steering wheel with a marker.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being the fastest for one lap, it's about being the fastest over the long haul."
careerHighlight: Finishing 2nd overall in the 24 Hours of Daytona in 2023, showcasing his ability to perform under pressure in a grueling endurance race.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final hour of the 2022 24 Hours of Spa, costing his team a likely victory.
